brief: October was the worst month for momentum in more than 40 years: cap-weighted momentum underperformed the market by 10.8%, a -5.8 sigma event, including two 6-sigma unwind days within about a week. Long/short momentum lost 16% in the month. Combined with July, the cumulative drawdown reached 30%, the largest since ChatGPT launched, erasing a year of outperformance. Hedge fund losses: Equity Long/Short and Multi-Strat funds lost around 3%, Equity Quant funds 4-5%, Asia-focused Quant funds 7-8%, with Multi-Strat damage comparable to dot-com, Lehman and COVID. JPM argues forced AI-exposure liquidation may have exceeded July's. JPM's view: the liquidation has reset positioning, with momentum crowding down from the 100th to the 86th percentile historically and to the 12th percentile versus the past three years, creating a more favorable backdrop for equities, especially AI, so the next surprise could come from the upside. JPM does not expect hedge funds back in AI immediately, expecting a few weeks of retail-supported stability before institutions return from late November. The complication: retail is also slowing, with weekly flows down to $2.5bn versus a $6.5bn 12-month average and $2.3bn of single-stock outflows.
